source.title: Scaling Laws and Tradeoffs in Recurrent Networks of Expressive Neurons
source.authors: Aaron Spieler; Georg Martius; A. Levina

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling and budget-allocation patterns in ELM recurrent networks, a different architecture from the language-model scaling studies cited in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as background but reports no results from their parameter/token/compute sweeps. Its Enwik8 experiments measure held-out BPC while varying ELM neuron count, per-neuron complexity, connectivity, and architecture. It does not sweep training tokens or training compute as scaling variables, and does not test downstream-task predictability.
record.test_reason: On Enwik8 character-level language modelling, ELM recurrent networks are swept over parameters along several architectural axes, with held-out test BPC measured. The study reports approximate power-law decay of reducible BPC along a Pareto recipe and fixed-budget shape tradeoffs. This bears on V1, V4 and V7 in a new architecture. Data and training steps are fixed throughout, and no token or compute sweep is done.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that the simple-unit default in ML is not obviously optimal, and that complex per-unit machinery is a budget-efficient design choice. They state the Pareto recipe is predicted to fail once neurons reach their noise floor, a regime not yet reached.
record.recipe_differences: Uses recurrent ELM networks and architectural sweeps over neuron count, per-neuron complexity, and connectivity, rather than language-model parameter/token/compute scaling fits or Kaplan/Hoffmann compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The Enwik8 scaling slope changes with connectivity and synaptic-integration hierarchy; the preferred recurrence fraction changes with network size; the exact fixed-budget optimum shifts with high-pass-filter timescale; and model/data-specific theory parameters and the noise floor affect the scaling curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Single ELM neuron fitted to NeuronIO membrane voltage: reducible MAE falls as a power law in per-neuron parameters over two orders of magnitude. Log decay is not ruled out (dAICc 0.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-unit approximation error scales as a power law in per-unit parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: An information-theoretic proxy with independently derived parameters predicts fixed-budget tradeoff curves at unseen budgets (r=0.9801).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Theory-derived proxies extrapolate budgeted architecture tradeoffs across modest budget changes.

record.problems: All results are for ELMs and ELM Networks except preliminary Transformer experiments. Enwik8 sweeps often report single-run results; the paper notes fixed training setup, nonuniform hardware and wall-time effects, possible missed configurations in the structured search, and uncertainty in independently measured theory exponents. Some values are available only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: SHD-Adding accuracy sweeps and NeuronIO single-neuron voltage-prediction error sweeps were not included as rows because they do not measure language-model held-out loss. The paper's quoted previous-work baselines and cited scaling-law results are not its own results.

untested.parts: No sweep over training tokens or compute. Data and steps are fixed, so data may bottleneck the larger models. Scale reaches only about 3e7 parameters.
No small-run power-law fits extrapolated orders of magnitude. Fig 22 theory-proxy extrapolation covers only about 8x in budget.
No image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regimes. Only the SHD-Adding spiking-audio classification task is tested.
No comparison of Kaplan vs Hoffmann fitting procedures or parameter counting.

missing.what: SHD-Adding Pareto-recipe reducible-error scaling (approximate power law), bearing on V5
Budget type changes the optimum: ISO-FLOPs is essentially unchanged; ISO-wall-time shifts the optimum toward larger neurons
Two-hidden-layer, same-budget network: overall degradation, with the optimum shifted to smaller neurons
Authors state the fixed training setup and hardware misalignment bias the exact exponents and optima

record.verdict_notes: All sweeps use fixed data (Enwik8) and a fixed training setup, so the results speak to parameter scaling only. Models are small, at most about 3e7 parameters. Most Enwik8 values are figure-only and single-run. R3, R5 and R6 were relinked to V4 as fixed-parameter shape comparisons. 'Reversed' states for R7 and R8 were changed to 'absent' (the small-effect claim fails rather than inverts).

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep over training tokens or training compute; model size is explored through ELM architecture dimensions rather than a conventional language-model parameter-count sweep.

The paper predicts tradeoffs at other parameter budgets using an information-theoretic proxy, but does not test power-law fits from small language-model runs predicting runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute allocation between language-model parameters and training tokens is tested.
The paper tests selected ELM architecture changes and an attention head-count/head-size tradeoff, not a comprehensive range of depth, width, and architecture designs.
The language-model experiment uses text; no other modality, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer setting is tested.
No downstream-task performance is measured against scale or pretraining loss.
The paper examines setup-dependent scaling behavior in ELM networks, but does not compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann language-model fitting procedures or establish why their published laws disagree.

rows.size_stated: Nrec sweep spanning over an order of magnitude
rows.operation_detail: Varied recurrent neuron count on Enwik8 and measured test BPC.

conditions.value: constant ds or proportional ds variants shown

rows.value: Figure only; text reports monotonic improvement with neuron count over more than an order of magnitude.
rows.note: The text says the improvement slope is faster when input connections increase in proportion to neuron count; this is not reported as a power-law fit.
rows.check: Monotonic BPC improvement with Nrec over about one order of magnitude, but no power-law fit is reported. The slope depends on the connectivity rule, so the row also bears on V7. The reader linked only V1, which is why the V7 label flagged R1.

source_check.correct: V1: cannot_determine from the reported monotonic trend alone; no power-law fit is reported for this neuron-count sweep. V7: observed connectivity-dependent scaling slopes.
source_check.problem: Monotonic improvement without a power-law assessment does not establish that V1 holds partially.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.size_stated: Neuron complexity sweep spanning over an order of magnitude
rows.operation_detail: Varied per-neuron memory complexity and measured Enwik8 test BPC.

conditions.value: constant ds and proportional ds variants shown

rows.value: Figure only; text reports monotonic improvement with neuron complexity, with slower improvement for lmlp = 0 and faster improvement with proportional ds.
rows.note: The study says the architecture choices alter scaling slopes, including after accounting for total parameters.
rows.check: Monotonic improvement with ke, with no power-law fit. The slope depends on the integration hierarchy. Not a fixed-parameter shape comparison, so V4 removed.

source_check.correct: Figures 4b and 9b compare lmlp=1 and lmlp=0; constant versus proportional connectivity belongs to the neuron-count panels. These panels report monotonic improvement and hierarchy-dependent slopes, without determining V1's functional form. Separate complexity power-law fits appear in Figure 6g and Appendix A.4.
source_check.problem: The connectivity variants are assigned to the wrong sweep; the partial V1 state is not established by monotonicity.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.operation_detail: Varied neuron count and complexity under fixed parameter budgets.
rows.value: Figure only; text reports a non-trivial interior optimum at each budget, with larger budgets favoring more numerous and more complex neurons.
rows.note: This is an allocation tradeoff among ELM architecture dimensions, not a parameter-versus-token compute-optimal split.
rows.check: Fixed-budget N vs ke tradeoff with an interior optimum and a steep drop-off at the extremes. This is a shape-at-fixed-parameters result, not a power-law loss result, so relinked from V1/V7 to V4. Loss differences near the optimum are figure-only.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.operation_detail: Varied synapse connectivity and compared recurrent and feed-forward connection changes.
rows.value: Figure only; text reports that more synapses improve performance, that too few of either connection type cause a marked drop, and that additional recurrent connections account for almost all benefit after feed-forward connections are sufficient.
rows.note: Reports connection-type-dependent effects rather than a universal small effect of architecture details.
rows.check: Connectivity sweep changes the parameter count, so it is not fixed-P and V4 is removed. Improvement is monotonic; gains depend on recurrent vs feed-forward connections.

source_check.correct: The connectivity sweep establishes monotonic gains, saturation of feed-forward benefits, and continued gains from recurrent connections. V1's power-law form cannot be determined from these qualitative results.
source_check.problem: The absence of a power-law fit does not establish a partial power law.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.operation_detail: Varied the recurrent fraction of neuron inputs.
rows.value: Figure only; text reports that larger networks favor higher recurrence.
rows.note: The preferred recurrent fraction changes with network size.
rows.check: The recurrent-fraction optimum shifts with network size. Magnitudes are figure-only. V7 link dropped: this is not an exponent or fit result.

source_check.correct: The preferred recurrent fraction rises with network size. V4 state: cannot_determine from the stated optimum shift alone, because the loss differences are not quantified in the text.
source_check.problem: An optimum shifting with scale does not by itself show that architecture changes loss more than slightly.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.operation_detail: Varied the split between per-neuron complexity parameters and connectivity parameters.
rows.value: Figure only; text reports an optimum around Nrec connections.
rows.note: The optimum is specific to the tested connection/complexity allocation.
rows.check: Per-neuron ke vs kc split at fixed parameters gives an optimum near Nrec connections. Magnitude is figure-only.

source_check.correct: The complexity/connectivity allocation has an optimum around Nrec connections. V4 state: cannot_determine from the reported optimum alone; its loss magnitude is figure-only.
source_check.problem: The existence of an optimum alone does not establish a partial failure of V4's small-effect claim.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.size_stated: Parameter-matched configurations; exact sizes not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron integration hierarchy and network configuration at matched total parameter counts.

conditions.value: Total parameters accounted for in the comparison

rows.baseline: Simpler synaptic integration, lmlp = 0; exact value not stated
rows.value: Figure only; hierarchical synaptic integration performs substantially better, even accounting for total parameters.
rows.note: Contradicts the claim that architecture details change loss only slightly in this tested comparison.
rows.check: At matched total parameters, lmlp=0 is worse 'by a large margin' (Fig 9b), so a small architecture effect is absent here. The record's 'reversed' misstates the state. This is a functional change to neuron integration rather than pure depth/width.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.size_stated: Parameter-matched configurations; exact sizes not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Compared feed-forward ELM networks and networks with two hidden layers under the same parameter budget.
rows.baseline: Single-hidden-layer recurrent reference; exact value not stated
rows.value: Figure only; text reports that performance degrades substantially, about 0.1 test BPC, for the altered configurations, while the interior tradeoff remains.
rows.note: The architecture changes have a non-negligible loss cost in these parameter-matched comparisons.
rows.check: Feed-forward variant (rho_rec=0) degrades about 0.1 test BPC; the two-hidden-layer variant degrades with no number given. The 0.1 figure applies to the feed-forward panel only. 'Reversed' is wrong.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.operation_detail: Varied high-pass filter timescale and measured fixed-budget neuron-count/complexity tradeoffs.
rows.baseline: Reference τr = 2; exact baseline value not stated
rows.value: Figure only; text reports similar qualitative tradeoffs across tested timescales, but the exact optimum shifts with timescale.
rows.note: Large-neuron configurations benefit from faster readout timescales and small-neuron configurations from slower ones.
rows.check: tau_r is a neuron filter hyperparameter, not model shape. The row reports robustness of the tradeoff, not a loss-scaling claim.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.operation_detail: Measured reducible Enwik8 test BPC as per-neuron effective parameter count increased at fixed layer width.
rows.measure: Reducible test BPC versus per-neuron parameters ke
rows.baseline: Reference floor of 0.97 BPC for reducible BPC calculation
rows.value: Figure only; additive-floor and max-floor models are preferred over pure power law or log decay, and are not significantly distinguishable from each other.
rows.uncertainty: AICc values shown in figure: log decay 13.2; power law 20.8; additive floor 0.0; max floor 2.6.
rows.note: The paper identifies a knee/noise-floor regime, so a single power law does not describe the whole sweep.
rows.check: At fixed width N=1024, reducible BPC vs ke prefers floor models: dAICc is 0 and 2.6 for floor models vs 20.8 for a pure power law. The curve bends away from a single power law, a per-neuron noise floor rather than data limits.

rows.subject: ELM Network
rows.size_stated: Three orders of magnitude in trainable parameters
rows.operation_detail: Searched joint neuron-count and internal-dimension configurations and evaluated a one-variable scaling recipe.

conditions.value: dm ∼ Nrec; dmlp = 2dm; dtree = 2dmlp; dbranch = dtree; ρrec ∼ Nrec/(Nrec + dinp)

rows.measure: Reducible task error and reducible BPC along the Pareto frontier
rows.value: The recipe traces the empirical Pareto frontier across both datasets and three orders of magnitude in trainable parameters; its reducible-error decay is described as approximate power-law behavior.
rows.uncertainty: Pareto candidates: mean and standard deviation across five runs; other SHD-Adding results use three runs and Enwik8 results are single runs.
rows.note: The authors say the power-law-like recipe is expected to stop applying once larger neurons reach their individual noise floor; that regime was not reached.
rows.check: Approximate power-law decay of reducible error along the Pareto recipe. On Enwik8 this spans only about 1.5 orders (about 1e6 to 3e7 parameters); three orders holds only across both datasets. The SHD-Adding part bears on V5. Enwik8 non-Pareto points are single runs, and the reducible-BPC floor of 0.97 is taken from prior work.

source_check.correct: The joint recipe uses dm proportional to sqrt(Nrec), with dmlp=2dm, dtree=2dmlp and dbranch=dtree. Appendix A.3 specifies a square-root recurrence rule for SHD-Adding and Nrec/(Nrec+dinp) for Enwik8. Reducible metrics use stated reference floors: approximately 0.116 task error for SHD-Adding and 0.97 BPC for Enwik8.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3, paragraph following Figure 7; Appendix A.3, Table 3 and configuration details; Appendix A.2
source_check.problem: The recipe loses square roots in text extraction, and the reducible-metric reference floors are omitted.

relation.reason: Its own loss, error, architecture sweeps and fitted curves bear directly on several claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study tests scaling and architecture tradeoffs in expressive recurrent networks and a non-text sequence task, extending the setting of the claims.

source_check.notes: The extracted recipe displaces square-root symbols; read Section 4.3 together with Appendix A.3. Three orders of parameter range describes the combined datasets; the predicted Pareto-recipe noise-floor breakdown was not reached.

statements.correction: Figure 9b: hierarchical integration substantially outperforms simpler integration after accounting for parameters. Figure 12a: feed-forward penalty approximately 0.1 test BPC. Figures 4c,e,f: allocation optima. Figure 4d: too few recurrent or feed-forward connections sharply degrades performance while parameter count varies. Figure 23a: interior Transformer optima at fixed attention budgets.

The text does not establish steep fixed-budget extremes for every recurrence and connectivity allocation sweep; the explicit connectivity drop-off also comes from a sweep that changes parameter count.
